newsitem.title: USA: Smithfield Foods sees Lykes profit.
newsitem.headline: Smithfield Foods sees Lykes profit.

text.p: Smithfield Foods Inc said Thursday it expects its Lykes Meat Group, acquired in November 1996, will operate profitably by the end of the current fiscal year.

Smithfield attributed its improved financial results to the inclusion of the third quarter results of John Morrell & Co, acquired in December 1995, and a substantial increase in profitability at the company's hog production group.
Offsetting these positives were sharply lower fresh pork results, a loss at Lykes Meat Group and weather-related plant shutdowns and inefficiencies at John Morrell in January, the company said.
Smithfield said it sharply reduced operating costs at Lykes and increased its domestic and international business. As a result, the company made its profitable prediction for Lykes.
Separately, the company said the pork processing industry "is plagued by excess slaughter capacity" and a shortage of live hogs.
At the same time, it said that several Midwestern competitors have increased capacity despite the reduced number of hogs available for slaughter in the region.

"This combination has pressured hog prices to exceptionally high levels at a time when cattle, as a result of the cyclical nature of that industry, are relatively plentiful at rather low prices," said Joseph Luter, Smithfield's chairman and chief executive officer. "Thus, pork is at a competitive disadvantage with beef and is not being featured as regularly at the retail level."
This, he said, accounts for continued losses in fresh pork operations at Smithfield and elsewhere.
